question: What is the late withdrawal policy?
final_answer:
I'm happy to help! As the La Trobe University Policy Assistant, I'll provide an answer using only the exact policy text provided.

The late withdrawal policy is not explicitly stated in the given context. However, we can look at related policies that might be relevant.

From [CHUNK 2] Admissions Procedure > Section 6 - Procedures > Part E - Withdrawal, Cancellation or Variation of Offers, we see that there are three scenarios for withdrawing an offer:

1. a transfer from the original course into a new course structure;
2. entry into an alternative course;
3. withdrawal of the offer and a refund of any fees paid.

However, this policy does not specifically address late withdrawals.

From [CHUNK 3] Student Fees Procedure - Remission of Debt or Fee Liability > Section 6 - Procedures > Part B - Applications for Remission > Timing of Applications, we see that there are two scenarios for applying for remission:

1. within 12 months of the subject withdrawal date, or, if the person could not withdraw;
2. within 12 months of the end of the teaching period in which the subject was, or was to be, undertaken.

Again, this policy does not explicitly state a late withdrawal policy.

question: How do I apply for special consideration?
final_answer:
To apply for special consideration, you need to submit your application in a timely manner, which means you can do so up until 11.59pm (Melbourne time) on the due date of your assessment. If you haven't already, you will be reminded to apply for a Short Extension first. If you believe you need more than a Short Extension, you can still apply for special consideration after receiving the Short Extension. 

Make sure to include all necessary information in your application. If you have any questions or need assistance, consider reaching out to your faculty's Student Administration office for support. Good luck!
